source_text: Ὅτι οὐ δεῖ ἐν τοῖς Κυριακοῖς, ἢ ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις, τὰς λεγομένας ἀγάπας ποιεῖν, ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐσθίειν, καὶ ἀκούβιτα στρωννύειν.
thought_title: No love feasts in church buildings
orientation: The council continues its rules on love feasts, now forbidding them inside church buildings.
pass_a_gloss: That it is not necessary on the Lord's days, or in the churches, to hold the so-called love feasts, to eat in the house of God, and to spread dining couches.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'love feast' for ἀγάπη in this communal-meal sense.
Latin loanword accubita meaning reclining couches for dining; 'dining couches' conveys the furniture sense.
The verb means to spread or lay out coverings or couches; 'spread' keeps the physical action.
The impersonal δεῖ with negative expresses prohibition ('one must not'); 'it is not necessary' is the literal force.

pass_b_english: One must not hold the so-called love feasts on the Lord's days or in churches, nor eat in the house of God, nor spread dining couches.

last_rejected.quote: nor eat in the house of God, nor spread dining couches
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐσθίειν, καὶ ἀκούβιτα στρωννύειν
last_rejected.why: English adds 'nor' before 'eat,' making three separate prohibitions; Greek has two: not hold love feasts in churches, and (while doing so) not eat in God's house or spread couches.
last_rejected.fix: One must not hold the so-called love feasts on the Lord's days or in churches, eating in the house of God and spreading dining couches.
last_rejected.ruling: οὐ δεῖ governs all three infinitives; καὶ connects final item in series, not a separate two-part prohibition.

last_rejected.why: τοῖς Κυριακοῖς means the Lord's houses (church buildings), parallel to churches, not Sundays.
last_rejected.fix: One must not hold the so-called love feasts in the Lord's houses or in churches, nor eat in the house of God, nor spread dining couches.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐν τοῖς Κυριακοῖς is neuter plural 'the Lord's (places/things)'; here parallel with ἐκκλησίαις, so 'Lord's houses' is plausible, but 'Lord's days' is within range and ambiguous, so not a clear major error.
